newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-VELEZ BEAT CRUZEIRO WITH PENALTY BY GOALKEEPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VELEZ BEAT CRUZEIRO WITH PENALTY BY GOALKEEPER.

text.p: Velez Sarsfield goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert scored his third goal in this year's South American Supercup as the Argentines beat Brazil's Cruzeiro 1-0 away in the first leg of the final on Wednesday.
Chilavert, whose goalkeeping abilities were barely tested by a subdued Cruzeiro attack, strode up to convert a penalty four minutes from the end, blasting his shot into the goal off the crossbar.
The game, played in driving rain, appeared to be heading for an insipird 0-0 draw until Cruzeiro defender Celio Lucio hauled down Patricio Camps in the penalty area.
The previous best opportunity had also fallen to the Paraguayan international goalkeeper, who fired over a free kick from the edge of the Cruzeiro penalty area midway through the second half.
Chilavert's previous goals in the competition, in which he is his team's topscorer, came from a free kick and a penalty.
He has also scored five times this year in the Argentine championship and once for his country in the South American World Cup qualifying competition.
Cruzeiro, twice Supercup champions, were backed by a 61,000 crowd but simply had no idea what to do with the ball when they got near the Argentine penalty area.

Velez were happy to defend early on and Chilavert was booked for time-wasting as early as the 30th minute, taking too long over a goal kick. Three other players from Velez and three from Cruzeiro were booked in a rough game.
The Argentines became more adventurous as the game went on and Wednesday's result makes them hot favourites to win the title, with the second leg in their own stadium on December 4.
